title: GREATGAME instance
description: One annotated canon-consistency instance. Formalizes section 4 of benchmark/greatgame-v0.1.md.

class.description: Instance class per section 5. Target distribution: conflict ~40%, supersession ~20%, apparent ~30%, uncovered ~10%.

constraint_type.description: Spec section 2 constraint type. Required when class is 'conflict'; meaningless otherwise.

assertions.description: The textual assertions in tension. An 'uncovered' instance carries exactly one — the candidate assertion the corpus never addresses.

source.description: Jay Finley Christ four-letter abbreviation. Non-negotiable — it is how the scholarly community this dataset rests on cites.

char_span.description: Authoritative locator into the pinned, checksummed edition. Character offsets rot silently if the edition is not pinned — see corpus.json.

excerpt.description: Short locator excerpt only. Never a passage.

authority.description: Spec section 1.2 authority tier. Two sources disagreeing is a conflict only at equal binding force.

narrator_belief.description: True when the assertion reflects what the narrator believed at the time rather than what the text asserts as fact. This field is what lets a system reason about supersession correctly.

explicit.description: False when the assertion must be inferred rather than read.

gold_verdict.description: Adjudicated verdict. Note 'apparent' instances carry gold_verdict 'conform' — the class describes the trap, the verdict describes the truth.

hazards.description: Drives Task A error analysis. Per-hazard recall is reported separately: 'recall is 0.71' is a number; 'recall collapses to 0.34 on temporal inference' is a paper.

resolution.description: Required when class is 'apparent'. Why the apparent conflict resolves — different referent, different time, different speaker.

explanatory_passage.description: Required when class is 'supersession'. The in-world explanation of the change.

scholarly_treatments.description: Paraphrased summaries with attribution. Never reproduced argument text — verbatim scholarly text is a defect in the dataset, not a citation.

summary.description: Written in the annotator's own words.

accepted_by_annotators.description: A contradiction scholars have explained away is still a contradiction in the text. A treatment being accepted does NOT change gold_verdict — it populates the resolutions array, which is a different thing.

annotation.description: Provenance of the label itself. Two independent annotators, disagreements adjudicated in a third pass and recorded rather than erased.

held_out.description: True for the 10-instance held-out split, published as hashes only.
